_comment: B2 spec/eval pilot (decisions/0011, 0037, 0073). Scoped to the pure catalog-backed validators -- validateSecurityTxt, validateLlmsTxt, validateFeedJson, validateFeedXml -- plus, since atlas decision 0122 phase 4 (executed by 0128), the pure llms coherence evaluator and tri-state fold that folded into b2-llms.mjs from audits/lib/llms-coherence.ts and audits/lib/llms-issue-outcome.ts. Network-path plumbing remains bracketed with '// Stryker disable all' / '// Stryker restore all' comments. This keeps the score about pure, declared logic instead of diluting it with untested I/O. thresholds.break=70 is the historical raise-only floor. Known survivors are primarily message StringLiteral mutants, because {id, severity} pairs are the catalog contract. Raise thresholds.break as cases are added; do not lower it to make a regression pass.
_comment_fold: THE FOLD MOVED ~260 MUTANTS UNDER THE GATE, AND THE PERCENTAGE FELL. Measured on the same three entries, same test suite: before, b2-llms.mjs scored 3 mutants (267 Ignored inside the disabled bracket, 3 Killed, 0 Survived) because the coherence evaluator and the fold lived in audits/lib/ files that were never in 'mutate' and therefore carried NO local mutation coverage; after, it scores 265 (281 Ignored, 194 Killed, 1 Timeout, 68 Survived, 2 NoCoverage). Project score 79.79% -> 76.71%. That is a denominator effect, not a regression: 195 more mutants are killed than before, and 262 newly-scored mutants were previously invisible here. The folded code is placed ABOVE the 'Stryker disable all' marker deliberately -- putting it below would have held the percentage at 79.79% while scoring nothing new, which is the number looking better than the coverage. thresholds.break stays 70 and is NOT lowered. The 68 survivors are led by StringLiteral (23), ObjectLiteral (11) and ConditionalExpression (8): the documented message-string class, since the coherence tests assert finding ids and artifact identity rather than prose.
_comment_plugins: REQUIRED under pnpm (atlas decision 0032). Stryker's default plugin discovery globs `@stryker-mutator/*` under the node_modules that contains @stryker-mutator/core -- under npm's flat tree that is the project root, where the vitest runner also sits, so discovery worked implicitly. pnpm's isolated layout puts core under node_modules/.pnpm/@stryker-mutator+core@<hash>/node_modules/, whose sibling @stryker-mutator/ directory holds only core's own deps, so the glob finds nothing and the run dies with 'Cannot find TestRunner plugin "vitest". In fact, no TestRunner plugins were loaded.' Naming the plugin explicitly resolves it from the project root instead of by glob. Do not remove.
_comment_llms_structure: scripts/audit/lib/llms-structure.mjs was the fourth entry here (143 mutants: 110 killed, 2 timeout, 31 survived, 78.32% on its own) until atlas decision 0079 item 4 wave 2b replaced the vendored copy with @j0nathan-ll0yd/estate-contracts. It is dropped rather than repointed: Stryker mutates a sandbox copy of the project and symlinks node_modules, so a mutate glob into a dependency is not supported and would write into the real install. THIS IS A REAL LOSS OF LOCAL SIGNAL AND IS NAMED, NOT HIDDEN -- the rule's mutation coverage is now atlas's to own. The rule is still behaviorally gated here by audits/__tests__/spec-cases.test.ts, b2-validate-llms-txt.property.test.ts and llms-differential.test.ts, and by the spec-version assertion in llms-structure.integrity.test.ts; it is simply no longer mutation-scored here. Measured effect on the gate: 78.80% over four files becomes 79.11% over three, so thresholds.break stays at its historical 70 floor and is NOT lowered.
